verdict: THE OUTCOME VARIABLE IS BARELY RELIABLE, AND THAT CAPS EVERY SEARCH BUILT ON IT. Split-half reliability of the per-prompt attribution drop is 0.302-0.422 at full length across two independent samples. Observed correlations are attenuated by sqrt(reliability) ~ 0.55-0.65, so a TRUE correlate of 0.30 shows up as roughly 0.17-0.20 and a true 0.50 as 0.28-0.33. At n=250 the smallest true correlation distinguishable from zero is about 0.23. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SIX NULLS: r40, r41, r46, r47, r54, r55 and r56 did not show that no mechanism explains r12's per-prompt pattern. They showed that no mechanism with a TRUE per-prompt correlation above roughly 0.2 does. A moderate real mechanism would have been invisible to every one of them. NOT A RESCUE OF ANY PARTICULAR MECHANISM: the two that failed to REPLICATE (entry 48, r56) failed against their own preregistered intervals, which is a different and stronger kind of failure than being underpowered.
outcome_variable_scope: The quantity whose reliability is measured is itself scored by the r08 model gold head (entry 50). This is the reliability of a proxy-world outcome.
scope: Reliability is not validity -- a perfectly reliable measure can still measure the wrong thing. The 6 pairs come from 4 responses and carry transitivity constraints, so the halves are not strictly parallel and Spearman-Brown is an approximation. A DIFFERENCE of two accuracies is inherently less reliable than either.
